findings.reason: adding a §7 followup carrying its `/reckon-build … §7` prompt makes the still-open section reachable by the next-step chain, which today it is not.
findings.text: §7 is declared `implementable` yet the followups block (`f-hsrs-002`, data-recommends-skill "...§6") supplies the one-line §05 invocation only for §6, so `roadmap`/`followup` readers see §6's build prompt but no driver for §7's resume-policy work

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew_run_commands.py`, `crew_resume`, `crew_redispatch`, `change_lane` and `resume_plan` all resolve in the tree, the new test path is a declared deliverable, and the evidence-archive anchors `#s2`, `#s3`, `#s4-queued-move`, `#s4-review-reflex`, `#s5` all resolve in `docs/evidence/archive/a-held-session-routes-to-a-serving-lane-landed.html` (the `audit-doc` dangling-link warns are a corpus-scope artifact — the evidence file exists and carries each id).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §6 and §7 each state a measurable done-when with a declared negative control (the lane-family pin failing on an unchanged-backend return; the resume cases reading the base value once `crew_resume` passes an empty override tuple again).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §7's control is logged under the run directory, a durable path that survives the run, not a node-local temp tree.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §7's write paths (`reckon/crew_run_commands.py`, `tests/test_a_resume_runs_under_its_dispatch_policy.py`) carry no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag, and the section's prose names mechanisms rather than tracker entries.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §7's stated root cause matches the code it cites: `crew_resume` resolves flight with an empty override tuple (`reckon/crew_run_commands.py:1295`) where `crew_redispatch` reads `dispatch_options.overrides` (`reckon/crew_run_commands.py:1407-1409`), both reaching `change_lane`/`resume_plan` (the two and only two `change_lane` callers), so the mechanism runs on the named production caller and produces the done-when.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §7 carries one deliverable (resume resolves its flight with the run's recorded overrides through one shared reading).
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §7 is declared `implementable` but the followups block carries a driving invocation only for §6 (`f-hsrs-002`), so the plan's next-step chain names no `/reckon-build … §7`.
